output.brief: What is driving the gap: most of it appears to be eligibility, not location. The promotion rule requires 18 months in level, and far fewer remote staff meet it (32% vs 74% of office staff). Among employees who are eligible, remote and office promotion rates are nearly the same (20.0% vs 21.1%). That residual difference is small and could be chance with only 110 remote people. So the data do not support proximity bias as the main cause, and the COO's three-day office rule would not fix a tenure problem. Confidence is moderate. Next steps: do not announce the attendance rule. Instead, report promotion rates within the eligible group, and check why remote staff have less time in level (for example, recent hiring). Also check stretch-assignment access and attrition, which I did not collect, before drawing firm conclusions on those points.
